newsitem.title: USA: Lucent responds to analyst's criticisms.
newsitem.headline: Lucent responds to analyst's criticisms.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc, responding to criticisms contained in a report by a Smith Barney analyst, Wednesday said it considers its accounting practices to be conservative.

In a report, Smith Barney analyst Anthony Langham criticized Lucent's "aggressive accounting practices (at least versus competitors' practices), certain sources of earnings, difficulty in getting answers to probing questions, and apparent problems in gross margin." Langham also downgraded his rating on the stock to neutral from outperform.
Lucent shares fell 4-1/2 to 54-1/8 in afternoon trading.
Lucent spokesman Dan Coulter said, "In general, we consider our accounting practices to be conservative." But he added, "Every analyst has a right to his or her opinion."

In particular, he said criticism of Lucent's financial disclosure policies in the Wall Street analyst's report failed to take account of the need to keep some financial results from its businesses secret for competitive reasons.

The analyst said he was concerned by Lucent's practice of booking no reserves for vendor financing risks in its Personal Communications Services (PCS) unit and for how it averages the cost of goods sold over the life of a contract instead of booking them in the quarter when goods ship.
"This policy overstates actual realized gross profit in the early stages of these contracts" and could penalize earnings in later stages of the contracts," Langham wrote.
Lucent officials denied many of the analyst's claims, saying it was based on an incomplete assesment of the company's finances.

"We do take reserves where they are appropriate but that doesn't always mean we announce those reserves," Coulter said. Lucent considers such details to be privileged information because it can be used to competitive ends by industry rivals.
Lucent maintained it uses conservative accounting practices and adheres to U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
"The way it's presented is misleading," Jim Lusk, a Lucent vice president and controller, said of the Smith Barney report. "It's not like those are the only things going on."
"He has picked out two specific facts ... but there are a lot of other facts" that balance out the picture, Lusk said.
Coulter said 19 of the 27 analysts who follow Lucent maintain a buy or outperform rating its stock, with the rest holding neutral or negative opinions, according to Zack's.

Lusk noted that comparisons to rival telecom equipment suppliers such as Sweden's Ericsson and Finland's Nokia are complicated by the fact these European companies do not adhere to U.S. accounting principles.
